pairs: In tempore autem illo consurget Michaël princeps magnus,
“But at that time Michael will rise up, the great leader,
qui stat pro filiis populi tui:
who stands up for the sons of your people.
et veniet tempus quale non fuit ab eo ex quo gentes esse cœperunt usque ad tempus illud.
And a time will come, such as has not been from the time that nations began, even until that time.
Et in tempore illo salvabitur populus tuus,
And, at that time, your people will be saved,
omnis qui inventus fuerit scriptus in libro.
all who will be found written in the book.
Et multi de his qui dormiunt in terræ pulvere evigilabunt,
And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken:
alii in vitam æternam,
some to everlasting life,
et alii in opprobrium ut videant semper.
and others to a reproach that they will always see.
Qui autem docti fuerint, fulgebunt quasi splendor firmamenti:
But those who have taught will shine like the brightness of the firmament,
et qui ad justitiam erudiunt multos,
and those who instruct many towards justice,
quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates.
like the stars for unending eternity.
Tu autem Daniel,
But you, Daniel,
claude sermones, et signa librum usque ad tempus statutum:
close the message and seal the book, until the established time.
plurimi pertransibunt,
Many will pass through,
et multiplex erit scientia.
and knowledge will be increased.”
Et vidi ego Daniel,
And I, Daniel, looked,
et ecce quasi duo alii stabant:
and behold, similarly two others stood up,
unus hinc super ripam fluminis,
one over here, on the bank of the river,
et alius inde ex altera ripa fluminis.
and the other over there, on the other bank of the river.
Et dixi viro qui erat indutus lineis,
And I said to the man, who was clothed in linen,
qui stabat super aquas fluminis:
who stood over the waters of the river,
Usquequo finis horum mirabilium?
“How long will it be until the end of these wonders?”
Et audivi virum qui indutus erat lineis,
And I heard the man,
qui stabat super aquas fluminis,
who was clothed in linen,
cum elevasset dexteram
who stood over the waters of the river,
et sinistram suam in cælum,
when he had lifted his right hand and his left hand up to heaven,
et jurasset per viventem in æternum,
and had sworn by He who lives forever,
quia in tempus,
that it would be for a time,
et tempora,
and times,
et dimidium temporis.
and half a time.
Et cum completa fuerit dispersio manus populi sancti,
And when the dispersion of the hand of the holy people is completed,
complebuntur universa hæc.
all these things will be completed.
Et ego audivi,
And I heard
et non intellexi.
and did not understand.
Et dixi:
And I said,
Domine mi,
“My lord,
quid erit post hæc?
what will be after these things?”
Et ait:
And he said,
Vade,
“Go,
Daniel,
Daniel,
quia clausi sunt signatique sermones usque ad præfinitum tempus.
for the words are closed and sealed until the predetermined time.
Eligentur, et dealbabuntur,
Many will be chosen and purified,
et quasi ignis probabuntur multi:
and, as if by fire, they will be tested,
et impie agent impii,
and the impious will act impiously,
neque intelligent omnes impii:
and none of the impious will understand,
porro docti intelligent.
yet the teachers will understand.
Et a tempore cum ablatum fuerit juge sacrificium,
And from the time when the continual sacrifice will be taken away
et posita fuerit abominatio in desolationem,
and the abomination of desolation will be set up,
dies mille ducenti nonaginta.
there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
Beatus qui exspectat,
Blessed is he who waits
et pervenit usque ad dies mille trecentos triginta quinque.
and reaches until one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
Tu autem vade ad præfinitum:
But you, go, until the predetermined time,
et requiesces, et stabis in sorte tua in finem dierum.
and you will rest and will stand in your allotted place at the end of days.
